name: Construction
description: A business whose people are on a site rather than in a building, where the day is set by a programme of work and the hours that count are the ones spent on site. This preset suggests the modules a construction deployment usually needs, the structure a contractor is usually built from, the site working patterns, the leave types a site crew usually offers, and the views a project manager and a contracts manager read. It decides none of the things that depend on where the business is: leave entitlement, tax, contributions, break length, site safety limits and the pay period all come from a verified rule pack, and the currency is a placeholder the customer confirms.

modules.description: Employee records, the sites they are assigned to, the departments and the jobs.
The hours worked on site, which are the numbers a construction business is paid and judged on.
The working-time model on site: the week, the clock-in tolerance and the breaks.
Shift patterns and the roster that puts the right crew on the right site.
The leave a site crew takes and the cover that has to be arranged around it.
The pay run. It stays switched off until a verified rule pack is attached.
Site crews are hired by the week and by the project, and the paperwork has to keep up.
The site, cost and attendance figures a project manager reports on.
The site crew sees its own shifts and books its own hours.
A contractor's records arrive as files, from another system or from a spreadsheet.
Site inductions, certifications and the training record that has to be produced before someone goes on a site.
How many people a project needs, and when, once there is enough history.

workforce.description: How the workforce records are kept: the optional fields the tenant holds on a person and the way the organisation is described. The fields a contractor keeps on a person, including the site they are assigned to.

time_tracking.description: How the hours are recorded: A mobile clock-in on site, with the site geofence switched on so that the hours are recorded where the work was actually done. The break and rest rules the law sets are not here; they come from the attached rule pack.

time.description: The working-time model: the week starts on monday, a clock-in is accepted a short time either side of the shift, and the breaks are the ones the roster shows. The site break, the daily working-time limit and the minimum rest between two shifts come from the rule pack.

break_rules.description: The break the roster shows, for every site that has no rule of its own.

scheduling.description: The shift patterns a site runs: an early crew that opens the site, a day crew, a late crew that secures it and the weekend cover. The roster is published a week at a time. The working-time limit, the minimum rest between shifts and the number of days in a row that may be worked come from the rule pack.

shift_templates.name: Day Crew
shift_templates.description: The crew that works the day shift on a site.

shift_templates.name: Weekend Cover
shift_templates.description: The crew that covers the weekend programme.

leave.description: The leave a site crew takes and the approval it needs. The entitlement, the accrual rhythm, the carry-over and the right to be paid for unused leave are decided by the rule pack, not here.

leave_types.name: Annual Leave
leave_types.description: The holiday the site crew takes.

leave_types.name: Family Leave
leave_types.description: The absence that a family matter causes.

leave_types.name: Unpaid Leave
leave_types.description: The absence the crew takes and is not paid for.

payroll.description: The pay run a contractor expects: monthly, with the components the jurisdiction may require. Every rate and amount is left to the rule pack, so payroll stays disabled until a verified pack is attached to the tenant.

statutory_components.label: Income tax
statutory_components.description: The tax withheld from the employee's pay. The rate comes from the rule pack; the preset only names the component so the customer can see it.

statutory_components.label: Social contributions
statutory_components.description: The employer contribution the jurisdiction requires. The rate comes from the rule pack; the preset only names the component.

statutory_leave_pay.description: Which of the leave types above the tenant expects to be paid and which it expects to be unpaid. The fraction of pay a statutory leave attracts is set by the rule pack, not here.

recruiting.description: How a contractor hires: the standard offer letter, and the checks a candidate is asked to consent to. The consent scope and what a candidate must be told about the checks are set by the law of the tenant's jurisdiction, so the scope is left to the rule pack.

reporting.description: The site, cost and attendance figures a project manager reports on, and the exports behind them.

ess.description: The screens the site crew uses for itself: the shifts it works, the hours it books and the leave it asks for.

imports.description: How the contractor brings its own records in: the templates, the dry run and the confirmation before anything is written.

learning.description: The training a site requires before somebody may work on it: the inductions, the certifications and the record that proves they were done.

forecasting.description: How the contractor works out the crew it needs, once there is enough history to be worth forecasting.

organisation_templates.description: The structure a contracting business is usually built from: the commercial side, the site side and the functions that support both. The customer may rename, move or refuse any of it.

exclusions.name: Statutory leave entitlement and accrual
exclusions.description: How many days of leave an employee is entitled to, how the entitlement accrues, how much may be carried into the next year and whether unused leave may be paid out.
exclusions.reason: These are set by the law of the tenant's jurisdiction and differ from one country to the next. A preset has no jurisdiction, so it names the slot and leaves the number to a verified rule pack.

exclusions.name: Tax, contributions and the statutory pay components
exclusions.description: The deductions, allowances and employer contributions the jurisdiction requires, and the rates they are charged at.
exclusions.reason: A tax rate and a contribution percentage are the most tightly guarded numbers in the product. They live in a verified rule pack and nowhere else, and payroll stays disabled until one is attached to the tenant.

exclusions.name: Minimum wage and pay floors
exclusions.description: The lowest pay the tenant may offer, and the floor that applies to a grade, a contract type or a working time.
exclusions.reason: The floor is set by the jurisdiction and changes with it. The tenant's own pay structure may sit above it, but the preset may not state it.

exclusions.name: Working-time limits, break length and minimum rest
exclusions.description: The daily and weekly working-time limits, the length of a statutory break, whether the break is paid, the minimum rest between two shifts and the number of days in a row that may be worked.
exclusions.reason: Every one of these is a working-time rule of the jurisdiction. The preset leaves the slots open so that the rule pack fills them with the values that apply where the tenant actually is.

exclusions.name: Notice periods and termination
exclusions.description: The notice an employee or an employer must give, and what happens to the contract when it ends.
exclusions.reason: Notice is a jurisdiction rule, and in some places it depends on the length of service and the reason for the ending. The tenant decides what it will do, and the rule pack tells it what it must do.

exclusions.name: Background check consent and disclosure
exclusions.description: Which checks a candidate may be offered, what the candidate must be told about them and what the candidate has to consent to.
exclusions.reason: Data-protection and employment law usually set both the scope and the wording. The preset leaves the scope to the rule pack so that the tenant never offers a check it is not allowed to offer.

exclusions.name: Data protection and retention
exclusions.description: How long the tenant keeps each kind of record, which records it may keep at all, and what happens to them when a person asks for them to be erased.
exclusions.reason: The retention periods and the rights are a matter for the tenant's own policy and for the law that applies to it. The product supports the workflows; it does not decide the periods.

exclusions.name: Pay frequency and currency
exclusions.description: The preset carries a monthly pay cycle and a placeholder currency. The tenant confirms both, and the jurisdiction may restrict either.
exclusions.reason: The pay period and the currency are the tenant's own commercial choices, but the law of the jurisdiction constrains them, so the tenant has to confirm them rather than inherit them.

exclusions.name: Site safety rules and statutory training
exclusions.description: The safety rules, the minimum training for a site and the record that has to be produced before somebody is allowed on one.
exclusions.reason: Site safety law differs from one jurisdiction to the next and is enforced differently. The product keeps the training record; the rule pack and the tenant's own safety system decide what the rules are.

exclusions.name: Working-time limits and site rules
exclusions.description: The daily working-time limit on site, the length and payment of the site break, the minimum rest and the number of days in a row that may be worked.
exclusions.reason: These are working-time rules of the jurisdiction, and a site may have its own arrangements on top of them. The preset leaves the slots to the rule pack.
